docs.title: Why TinyOlly?
docs.text:
Why send telemetry to a cloud observability platform while coding? Why not have one on your desktop?

TinyOlly is a lightweight OpenTelemetry-native observability platform built from scratch to visualize and correlate logs, metrics, and traces. No 3rd party observability tools - just Python (FastAPI), SQLite, OpenAPI, and JavaScript.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
Ingest & compatibility - Native OTLP over gRPC and HTTP; works with any OTel Collector distro - Runs on Kubernetes (kind) in Colima on Apple Silicon, no Docker Desktop; pre-built images on Docker Hub - Bounded retention: 30-minute TTL and 256 MB database cap, both configurable

Explore your telemetry - Service catalog with RED metrics, and an interactive service dependency map - Distributed trace waterfall with correlated logs and a per-trace service map - Metrics Explorer with cardinality analysis and raw series - Deep links and click-to-copy IDs: share a URL that opens straight to a trace or span

Collector control - Collector presets applied from the UI via OpAMP: tail sampling, PII redaction, OTTL transforms, enrichment, metrics shaping, log dedup, derived-metric and routing connectors (docs)

AI & automation - MCP server: Claude Code, Zed or any MCP client can query traces, logs and metrics, render charts, and follow built-in investigation skills (docs) - REST API with OpenAPI documentation

Demos - Realistic demo: the upstream OpenTelemetry Demo (Astronomy Shop) with failure-injection flags (docs, scenarios) - TinyOlly AI SRE Agent: an agent on shift over the shop that triages, investigates, proposes fixes and writes postmortems, scored against injected faults (docs)

Built with Python (FastAPI), SQLite and JavaScript.

Local Development Only

TinyOlly is not designed to compete with production observability platforms! It's for local development only and is not focused on infrastructure monitoring at this time.

docs.title: Cardinality Protection
docs.text:
Span waterfall showing distributed trace complexity

TinyOlly includes built-in protection against metric cardinality explosion with a configurable limit on unique metric names.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY 1000 Maximum unique metric names SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS 1800 Data retention in seconds (alias: REDIS_TTL)

docs.title: Kubernetes Deployment
docs.text:
Update k8s/tinyolly-otlp-receiver.yaml:

env:
  - name: MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY
    value: "2000"  # Increase limit
  - name: SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS
    value: "3600"  # 1 hour retention

docs.text:

docs.title: Model and network
docs.text:
The default is a model on your LAN: built and tested with Qwen3.8 27B (q4, MTP) on one RTX 5090 box running Ollama.

If the agent cannot reach a model on your LAN, restart Colima from your own Terminal app (macOS grants local network access per app):

colima stop -p tinyolly && ./scripts/colima-up.sh

On the demo's flags, the shift uses the flagd-ui API inside the cluster, so changes apply at once.

docs.title: Choose a model
docs.text:
Preset Default model Enable it Local (Ollama), default qwen3.8:27b-mtp-q4_K_M SRE_LLM_URL (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and SRE_MODEL on k8s/06-rebuild+deploy-sre.sh (pass them on every run) OpenAI gpt-5 (SRE_OPENAI_MODEL) OPENAI_API_KEY in the secret below Claude claude-opus-5-5 (SRE_ANTHROPIC_MODEL) ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the secret below

Configured presets appear in the console's model picker; switching applies to the next investigation. SRE_PRESET=claude (or openai) starts on a cloud preset. Put the keys in a secret: kubectl create secret generic tinyolly-sre-llm --from-literal=ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=.... Claude uses the official SDK with refusal fallbacks (ANTHROPIC_EFFORT, default medium). Cloud presets send telemetry excerpts (span and service names, error messages) to the provider; the local default keeps everything on your network.

docs.title: The console
docs.text:
• Live stream (left): every step as it happens: signals, evidence, prompt, tool calls and results, finding. Click a line for the full text.
  • Investigations (right): a list with each incident's name, status and cause. Click one for the full investigation:
    • Triage: act now, watch or noise, and whether it would page (shadow mode: nothing is paged; the shift report scores it).
    • Conclusion with confidence, and the theories considered: confirmed ✓, ruled out ✗ with the deciding fact, or open.
    • Evidence trail: the cited trace and every query the agent ran; each chip opens that view in TinyOlly, and hovering shows the result.
    • Timeline: related change marker, detection, new symptoms, investigation, conclusion, fix, recovery.
    • Blast radius, proposed fixes, recovery result and time to resolve.
    • Write postmortem: a blameless draft (summary, impact, timeline, root cause, theories, 5 whys, evidence, action items) to copy or download as markdown.
  • Ask (bottom): free-form questions about your telemetry.

docs.title: Demo shift
docs.text:
The demo shift flips OpenTelemetry Demo feature flags on a timer, so problems come and go. All flags reset to off on start, stop and exit.

The agent is never told what was injected. It finds problems from telemetry alone. DEMO_ANNOUNCE=1 also publishes each flip as a change marker (flag paymentFailure: off -> 50%) it can read with what_changed, as a real flag system would.

Scenario Flag What the agent should find payment-degraded paymentFailure=50% checkout errors; the cause is payment payment-down paymentUnreachable=on hard dependency outage cart-flaky cartFailure=25% partial errors seen by several callers ad-failure adFailure=on errors in one service slow-images imageSlowLoad=5sec frontend latency, cause upstream slow-shipping intlShippingSlowdown=5sec latency on one path only catalog-lock productCatalogLockContention=on latency from the database catalog-bad-product productCatalogFailure=on errors on one product only recommendation-cache recommendationCacheFailure=on slow path, subtle traffic-flood loadGeneratorFloodHomepage=on load, not a bug: capacity quiet none control: the agent should open nothing

Scenarios are data: docker/apps/tinyolly-sre/sre/scenarios.json.

  • Order: random (never the same fault twice in a row, a quiet period every 4 faults; DEMO_SEED makes it repeatable), or fixed for a rehearsed demo: DEMO_SCRIPT=payment-degraded,slow-shipping,quiet k8s/06-rebuild+deploy-sre.sh --demo (the shift ends with the script).
  • Controls: POST /demo/start, /demo/pause, /demo/stop, /demo/reset (all flags off), /demo/trigger with {"id": "slow-images"}. GET /demo/status shows what runs; the header shows only demo: running · next fault in 2:40, so the room does not see the answer first.
  • Scores: Reveal scores marks each investigation against the injected fault: correct (service and cause), partial, wrong, false positive, no answer; faults with no incident count as missed. GET /demo/report is the shift report: counts, paging decisions, time to detect and resolve, tool calls and tokens. Samples are small, so it gives counts, not percentages.

Profiles. Quick is the default: a scenario takes about 2 minutes (all 11 in about 25).

Quick (default) Realistic (--realistic) Faults stronger variants (paymentFailure=90%, cartFailure=75%, 10sec slowdowns), 75-90 s each the variants in the table above, 4-6 min each Between faults 30 s cooldown and a clean cutoff (earlier telemetry is ignored), 20-30 s gap 2.5-3 min cooldown for errors to age out, 1-2 min gap Shop load the size profile's (15 or 40 users) the same Detection every 5 s; error rate, rate and p95 from the last 30 s of spans every 30 s; rate and p95 from the service catalog Change notes off (the model stays free for investigations) a change-risk note and a post-change check per flip

To tune without waiting, record a shift once (SRE_RECORD=/tmp/shift.jsonl) and replay it through the detectors in seconds or the model in minutes: see "Fast iteration" in the agent's README.

docs.title: How it decides
docs.text:
Detectors run without a model: error spans, error rate (per service and per operation), p95 latency, traffic drop, a service that stops reporting, error logs, mesh denials, and TinyOlly's storage pressure. Each service learns its normal; a change must hold for two polls. Signals on a service and its direct callers or callees join one incident, investigated from the deepest service. Settings are in the agent's README.

Guardrails: at most 8 tool calls and 120 s per investigation, 12 investigations an hour, read-only tools (not TinyOlly's docs or playbooks, which describe the demo's faults), and cited traces and services are kept only if they appeared in the evidence.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Synthetic faults are not production; a good score says little about real incidents.
  • With --realistic, several faults leave too little signal at the demo's low traffic to detect.
  • Two unrelated faults close together can merge into one incident through a shared caller such as frontend.
  • One model run at a time: a review can delay an investigation by up to a minute.

docs.title: 3. Add AI SRE
docs.text:
The agent watches TinyOlly. When something breaks, it investigates and proposes a fix. Fixes are never applied.

Designed for a model on your LAN

Put your Ollama address in SRE_LLM_URL. To use Claude or OpenAI instead, see AI SRE Details.

SRE_LLM_URL=http://<your-ollama-host>:11434/v1 ./k8s/06-rebuild+deploy-sre.sh
kubectl port-forward deploy/tinyolly-sre 7173:8080

Keep the port-forward running.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
The console at http://localhost:7173 says it is watching your telemetry. Give it a few minutes to learn what normal looks like.

docs.title: REST API & OpenAPI
docs.text:
OpenAPI documentation with interactive Swagger UI

TinyOlly provides a comprehensive REST API for programmatic access to all telemetry data in OpenTelemetry-native format.

docs.title: Interactive API Documentation
docs.text:
Access the auto-generated OpenAPI documentation: - Swagger UI: http://localhost:5005/docs - Interactive API explorer - ReDoc: http://localhost:5005/redoc - Alternative documentation - OpenAPI Spec: http://localhost:5005/openapi.json - Machine-readable schema

All APIs return OpenTelemetry-native JSON with: - Resources: service.name, host.name, etc. - Attributes: Metric labels and span attributes - Full Context: Trace/span IDs, timestamps, status codes

docs.title: API Endpoints Overview
docs.text:
The REST API provides endpoints for:

Endpoint Method Description /api/traces GET List recent traces with filtering /api/traces/{trace_id} GET Get detailed trace with all spans /api/spans GET List recent spans with filtering /api/logs GET Retrieve logs with trace correlation /api/metrics GET List metrics with type, unit, description and cardinality /api/metrics/query GET Time series for one metric, with resource.* / attribute.* filters and start/end /api/metrics/{name} GET Time series for one metric (no filters) /api/service-map GET Get service dependency graph (merge=false for the layered Istio view) /api/mesh-posture GET Istio mesh security posture: mTLS coverage, plaintext and denied edges /api/service-catalog GET List services with RED metrics /api/stats GET System stats and cardinality info /admin/stats GET Detailed admin statistics /health GET Health check endpoint

All endpoints return data in standard OpenTelemetry format, ensuring compatibility with OpenTelemetry tooling and standards.

docs.title: 4. Query Metrics
docs.text:
List the available metrics (metadata only), then fetch one metric's time series:

cURLPython 
# What metrics exist?
curl "http://localhost:5005/api/metrics?limit=100"

# Time series for one metric, last 10 minutes by default (start/end are Unix seconds)
curl "http://localhost:5005/api/metrics/query?name=http.server.duration"

# Filter by resource and metric attributes
curl "http://localhost:5005/api/metrics/query?name=http.server.duration&resource.service.name=frontend&attribute.http.method=GET"

import requests

base = 'http://localhost:5005'
for m in requests.get(f'{base}/api/metrics', params={'limit': 100}).json():
    print(f"{m['name']} ({m['type']}, {m['unit']}) services={m['services']}")

d = requests.get(f'{base}/api/metrics/query',
                 params={'name': 'http.server.duration', 'resource.service.name': 'frontend'}).json()
for s in d['series']:
    print(s['attributes'], [(p['timestamp'], p['value']) for p in s['datapoints'][-3:]])

docs.title: 6. Get Service Dependency Map
docs.text:
Retrieve the service dependency graph:

cURLPython 
curl http://localhost:5005/api/service-map

import requests

response = requests.get('http://localhost:5005/api/service-map')
graph = response.json()

print("Services:", len(graph['nodes']))
for node in graph['nodes']:
    print(f"  - {node['id']} ({node['type']}, role {node.get('role')})")

print("\nConnections:", len(graph['edges']))
for edge in graph['edges']:
    print(f"  {edge['source']} → {edge['target']} ({edge['value']} calls)")

Response Format: 

{
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "frontend", "label": "frontend", "type": "service", "role": "service", "metrics": {"rate": 12, "error_rate": 0.0}},
    {"id": "waypoint", "label": "waypoint", "type": "service", "role": "waypoint", "metrics": {}}
  ],
  "edges": [
    {
      "source": "frontend",
      "target": "waypoint",
      "value": 1523,
      "p95": 4.2,
      "req_rate": 3.1,
      "error_count": 0,
      "source_kind": "traces+metrics",
      "mtls": true,
      "denied_count": 0
    }
  ]
}

  • role is service, waypoint, gateway or ztunnel (detected from the node name).
  • source_kind says where the edge came from: traces, metrics (Istio istio_tcp_* / istio_requests_total metrics, so a mesh with only ztunnel still has a map) or traces+metrics.
  • mtls is true/false from Istio's connection_security_policy, or null when no mesh metrics cover the edge.
  • denied_count counts denied calls: HTTP 403, gRPC status 7 (PERMISSION_DENIED), or a waypoint local reply.
  • merge (default true) folds name.namespace proxy identities (for example waypoint.boutique) into the app node. Pass merge=false to keep them separate.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
TinyOlly is designed for local development:

  • Retention: records expire after 30 minutes by default (SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS), and the SQLite database is capped at 256 MB (MAX_DB_SIZE_MB); the oldest records are evicted first when it fills.
  • Cardinality protection limits unique metric names to 1000 (MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY).
  • Request size: OTLP ingest bodies and gRPC messages are size-capped so a runaway exporter cannot fill the database; very large single batches may need the caps raised (see the receiver's GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES).
  • List endpoints accept limit (max 5000).

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: TinyOlly is a local-only tool and has no authentication, CORS restrictions or origin checks. Do not expose it beyond your machine.

docs.title: Collector presets
docs.text:
TinyOlly ships a baseline collector config plus presets you can apply from the OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config tab (or POST /api/opamp/config). Each preset is a complete collector config in docker/otelcol-configs/templates/ whose first comment line is the blurb shown in the UI.

Baseline (every config): memory_limiter → resourcedetection (env, system) → batch; the debug exporter is basic verbosity.

Preset Components What you see sampling tail_sampling (errors, >500 ms, 10 % of the rest), probabilistic_sampler (logs 25 %), forward + spanmetrics Trace count drops ~90 %; every error trace is kept. RED metrics are computed before sampling, so rates stay accurate. pii-redaction redaction on traces, logs and metrics (emails, card numbers, bearer tokens, token= URL secrets, *password*/*secret*/*cvv*/*card number* keys), attributes (hash user.id, delete auth/cookie headers; traces and logs) user.email → ****, ?token=… masked, user.id hashed, log bodies masked, redaction.masked.count added. Card patterns only match real card formats (grouped digits, or contiguous Visa/MC/Amex/Discover), so epoch timestamps and numeric IDs are left alone. transform-ottl transform, filter, resource /users/123 → /users/{id}, JSON log bodies flattened to attributes, health checks and debug logs dropped, deployment.environment.name added. enrichment resource, groupbyattrs service.namespace, deployment.environment.name, collector.preset on everything. metrics-shaping deltatocumulative, filter, metricstransform, interval Delta inputs become cumulative, noisy runtime metrics dropped, labels aggregated, 30 s flush. logs-dedup transform, logdedup 60 identical logs → 1 record with dedup_count: 60. connectors-metrics spanmetrics (exemplars on), servicegraph, count, signaltometrics Extra derived metrics: service graph, span/log counts, span-duration histogram. connectors-routing routing, failover, attributes Error spans take their own pipeline (collector.route=errors); failover to a backup exporter. prometheus-remote-write prometheusremotewrite receiver Accepts Prometheus remote write on :19291.

templates/examples/incorrect.yaml is a deliberately broken config for demoing the UI validator; it is not listed as a preset.

docs.title: How configs are applied (important)
docs.text:
The OpAMP supervisor merges the remote config into the base config.yaml (maps are merged by key, lists replaced). Pipelines are therefore merged by name: a preset that only added traces/foo would leave the base traces pipeline running alongside it (so, e.g., sampling would be bypassed). Every preset defines its main pipelines as traces, metrics and logs, and extra pipelines with suffixes (traces/sampled). Keep that convention when writing your own.

Remote config is delivered at the agent's next OpAMP check-in, so a new preset can take ~10-30 s to become active (watch effective config on the Collector tab).

docs.title: Stability notes (collector-contrib 0.165.0)
docs.text: Alpha: filter, redaction (logs/metrics), logdedup, deltatocumulative, count/signaltometrics/routing/failover connectors, probabilistic_sampler (logs). Beta: tail_sampling, transform, memory_limiter, resourcedetection, groupbyattrs, metricstransform, cumulativetodelta. Stable: k8sattributes.

docs.title: Not included (yet)
docs.text:
• k8sattributes (needs RBAC + a Kubernetes cluster) and geoip (needs a MaxMind database) — would be a separate Kubernetes preset.
  • cumulativetodelta and metricstarttime are available in the image but not wired into a preset.
  • filelog receiver (needs file mounts).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
./scripts/test-collector-configs.sh        # validate + start every config with the pinned collector image
./scripts/sync-k8s-configs.sh              # regenerate Kubernetes ConfigMaps after editing configs/presets

docs.title: Development and testing
docs.text:
• Python dependencies are locked: edit requirements.in in a service directory, then regenerate with:

    uv pip compile requirements.in --universal --python-version 3.13 -o requirements.txt

  • Pinned versions (collector, supervisor, Ollama, OBI, Python, Go) live in versions.env; the Dockerfiles carry matching ARG defaults. Update both together.

  • The architecture diagram (docs/images/architecture.png) is generated by scripts/make-architecture-diagram.py: run it with docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/.venv/bin/python (needs matplotlib and Pillow).

  • Lint with the pinned ruff (rules in ruff.toml; its defaults change between releases). There is no CI, so run checks locally:

    pip install ruff==0.17.4
ruff check docker/apps/

  • All local tests: common, UI/API, receiver, MCP server, frontend JS (node --test), Go, collector configs, kubectl guard. --stack adds the e2e run against the running stack; --kind adds the kind smoke test (throwaway cluster; delete yours first):

    ./scripts/test-all.sh

  • Individual suites:

    (cd docker/apps/tinyolly-common && pip install -r requirements-test.txt . && pytest tests)

    ./scripts/test-go.sh
(cd docker/apps/tinyolly-ui && pytest tests)
./scripts/test-kubectx-guard.sh

  • End-to-end (stack up, ~8 min; --up starts it, --only a,b picks scenarios, --list shows them). It drives OTLP through the collector, applies every preset via OpAMP and checks results through the API (test hooks: POST /admin/reset, POST /api/opamp/config?wait=N):

    python3 scripts/e2e.py

  • OpenTelemetry Demo (demo running on kind, ~12 min; see Add the Demo): checks the data, the MCP tools, failure flags and the PII preset:

    scripts/test-otel-demo.py

  • Collector configs: ./scripts/test-collector-configs.sh (validate and start every preset); after editing them run ./scripts/sync-k8s-configs.sh.

  • Docs pages need title/description front matter (the MCP server lists them).

docs.title: Building and publishing images
docs.text:
The deploy script pulls images from Docker Hub (tinyolly/*). To run your own changes, build locally; to publish, use build/dockerhub/.

Goal Command Load core images into kind build/local/build-core-kind.sh Build and deploy the agent on kind k8s/06-rebuild+deploy-sre.sh [--demo] Log in to Docker Hub build/dockerhub/01-login.sh Build / push core (python-base, otlp-receiver, ui, mcp, opamp-server, otel-supervisor) build/dockerhub/02-build-core.sh <version> then 03-push-core.sh <version> Build / push only the UI (quick iteration) 02-build-ui.sh <version> then 03-push-ui.sh <version> Build / push the agent (tinyolly/sre) 02-build-sre.sh <version> then 03-push-sre.sh <version> Build / push everything 02-build-all.sh <version> then 03-push-all.sh <version>

Builds are native-architecture and uncached and tag latest plus the version; DOCKER_HUB_ORG overrides the organization. Publishing a GitHub release runs .github/workflows/release.yml, which runs 02-build-all.sh and 03-push-all.sh with the release tag. Details: build/README.md.

docs.title: Testing mesh features without Istio
docs.text:
scripts/seed_mesh.py posts synthetic Istio metrics (OTLP/JSON) for an Online Boutique mesh: scenarios baseline, flaky, fault, canary, deny, multicluster, plus --trace (a trace through a gateway and a waypoint), --l7 <service> and --ui <url> (records a change marker). With TinyOlly running on kind:

python3 scripts/seed_mesh.py --scenario flaky --ui http://localhost:5005
# then ask the MCP server (get_edge, what_changed, chart_map_diff)

docs.title: Agent eval
docs.text:
scripts/agent_eval/eval.py injects a known fault, lets a local model investigate through the MCP tools, and grades the answer against ground truth (service, cause, evidence). Five scenarios including a healthy control, on kind (real faults from the Istio demo repo). Needs Ollama (LOCAL_BASE, LOCAL_MODEL); results go to eval-results.json.

python3 scripts/agent_eval/eval.py --repeat 3
python3 scripts/agent_eval/eval.py --scenarios flaky,deny --no-skill-hint

pytest scripts/agent_eval

docs.title: Documentation images
docs.text:
Screenshots are generated, not hand-pasted. scripts/make-doc-images.py screenshots the UI tabs (headless Chrome) and saves the MCP chart images, each twice: a preview (max 900 px wide) in docs/images/ and the full size in docs/images/full/ (what a click opens). The OpenTelemetry Demo shots come from scripts/make-otel-demo-images.py.

scripts/make-doc-images.py                       # all shots from the running stack (UI :5005, MCP :8765)
scripts/make-doc-images.py --only mesh-map-diff  # one shot
scripts/make-doc-images.py --seed --otlp http://localhost:4318   # post a fault scenario first (diff and trace path)
scripts/make-doc-images.py --check               # no stack needed; also runs in test-all.sh

To add one, add a line to SHOTS, run the script, and embed it as [![alt](images/<name>.png)](images/full/<name>.png), or with a width, <a href="../images/full/<name>.png"><img src="../images/<name>.png" width="400"></a>. Path prefixes: markdown under docs/ uses images/ (MkDocs rewrites it); raw HTML uses ../images/ because pages are served at /<page>/ (except docs/index.md: images/); the README uses docs/images/. --check fails on a missing shot, a preview over 300 KB, or an embed without the click-to-expand link. Settings: TINYOLLY_UI, TINYOLLY_MCP, CHROME; needs Pillow or macOS sips.

Before publishing the docs site (./mkdocs-deploy.sh pushes to gh-pages):

  1. scripts/make-doc-images.py --check passes.

  2. The build is clean with warnings as errors (a "target is not found" warning means a wrong image path):

    source ~/.venv/mkdocs/bin/activate
python3 -m mkdocs build --strict -d /tmp/site

  3. Open the built page and click an image: python3 -m http.server -d /tmp/site 8000, then http://localhost:8000/<page>/.

Common mistakes: a wrong path prefix (see above), not committing docs/images/full/<name>.png (the click opens a 404), editing a generated preview by hand.

docs.title: What is running?
docs.text:
scripts/status.sh prints, read-only and in about four seconds, the Colima VMs, the kind cluster's namespaces, Helm releases and node memory, which stacks and demos are deployed with the command that removes each, TinyOlly's endpoints with their service counts, and disk use.

scripts/status.sh            # everything
scripts/status.sh --short    # skip the disk and node-memory details

docs.title: Tear everything down
docs.text:
scripts/teardown.sh removes what status.sh shows, in levels; each level includes the ones above it. It is destructive: it prints the plan and waits for y (or --yes).

scripts/teardown.sh --level demos      # OpenTelemetry Demo (Docker and kind), Istio ambient demo
scripts/teardown.sh --level stacks     # + TinyOlly itself, Docker and kind, data volumes included
scripts/teardown.sh --level cluster    # + the kind cluster
scripts/teardown.sh --level vms        # + stop the tinyolly Colima VM
scripts/teardown.sh --level vms --prune            # also prune build cache and dangling images first
scripts/teardown.sh --level vms --delete-vms --yes # delete the VMs and their disks (data loss)

It only touches what this project creates and lists other containers that would stop with a VM. --prune-images also removes all unused images.

docs.title: Docker contexts
docs.text: This project uses its own Colima VM, colima-tinyolly. Every script pins DOCKER_CONTEXT=colima-${COLIMA_PROFILE:-tinyolly}; new scripts that call docker must too (copy the block from build/local/build-core-kind.sh). Ad hoc: docker --context colima-tinyolly ....

docs.title: Service catalog actions (easy revert)
docs.text:
Per-service actions in the APM Service Catalog are a popover menu on the service name. To get back the old row of buttons, set ACTIONS_STYLE = 'buttons' at the top of docker/apps/tinyolly-ui/static/serviceCatalog.js and rebuild the UI:

build/local/build-core-kind.sh && kubectl rollout restart deploy/tinyolly-ui

To remove the menu code, delete SERVICE_ACTIONS, openServiceMenu, closeServiceMenu, the data-service-menu click handler and the two document.addEventListener lines. The map and catalog cross-links are independent of this setting.

docs.title: Istio Ambient Mesh
docs.text:
TinyOlly can show an Istio ambient mesh (no sidecars) on the service map. The ambient data plane splits in two:

  • ztunnel (one per node) gives every pod mTLS and L4 metrics, but emits no traces.
  • Waypoint (optional Envoy per namespace or service) adds L7 features and emits traces, access logs and request metrics.

Because ztunnel produces only metrics, TinyOlly builds map edges from Istio metrics as well as from traces.

Runnable demo

The istio-ambient-demo repo installs Istio ambient on a local kind cluster, deploys Online Boutique, and has scenarios for waypoint, canary, fault injection, retries and authorization policy. Its guide has a screenshot at each step and prompts for asking an AI assistant about the mesh through the MCP server. It is a separate repo so TinyOlly stays small.

docs.title: What you get on the map
docs.text:
Feature How it shows Topology without traces Edges from istio_tcp_connections_opened_total and istio_requests_total (source_kind: metrics) mTLS posture Green edges are mutual TLS, orange dashed edges are plaintext; the bar above the map shows mTLS 92.5% · 3 plaintext · 1 denied Denied calls Red thick edge. Counted from HTTP 403, gRPC status 7 (PERMISSION_DENIED), waypoint local replies, and L4 connections ztunnel refuses (response_flags=DENY, e.g. plaintext into a STRICT mTLS namespace) Mesh roles Waypoint (cut box) and gateway (pentagon) node shapes Merged vs Layered waypoint.boutique (trace identity) and waypoint (metric identity) merge into one node; untick Merge proxy and app nodes to see both

The same data is available from GET /api/service-map and GET /api/mesh-posture (API reference) and the get_service_map / get_mesh_posture MCP tools (MCP).

docs.title: Getting the data in
docs.text:
1. Metrics: scrape ztunnel and the waypoint (Prometheus port 15020) with an OpenTelemetry Collector prometheus receiver and forward the istio_* metrics to TinyOlly's OTLP receiver. The demo repo has a ready mesh-metrics.yaml.
  2. Traces (optional): register an OpenTelemetry extension provider in Istio and enable it with a Telemetry resource on the waypoint; the app's own spans stitch into the same traces if the app exports to TinyOlly too.
  3. Name your services consistently: edges from metrics use Istio's source_canonical_service / destination_canonical_service labels, so set OTEL_SERVICE_NAME in the app to the same name to join metric and trace edges.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Namespace merge: a name like waypoint.boutique is merged into waypoint only when boutique appears as a workload namespace in the mesh metrics.
  • Denial detection is heuristic: a gRPC call denied by an authorization policy returns HTTP 200 with grpc-status: 7, and a waypoint local reply shows up with no upstream workload. TinyOlly treats both as denied, and also connections ztunnel marks DENY. Calls that fail upstream with a response flag (for example UH) count as errors, not denials.
  • Plaintext edges are normal for non-mesh traffic such as apps exporting telemetry to TinyOlly.
  • History persists: ztunnel counters count from when ztunnel started, so TinyOlly shows denied and plaintext history from before a demo began. Restart ztunnel and clear TinyOlly's stored telemetry (POST /admin/reset) for a clean start.
  • Why did it break? get_edge decodes the response flags an edge carries (UC, UT, DI, DENY...) with a meaning and a next step, and what_changed lines up change markers (POST /api/events, which the demo's scenario script posts) with the failures and traffic around them.
  • Seeing the mesh: the map fades edges that only have connection counts (L4) when others have request data, shows each service's cluster and marks edges that cross clusters when the metrics carry cluster labels, and chart_map_diff / chart_trace_path show what changed and where one request spent its time. get_mesh_posture reports L7 coverage and the L4-only edges.
  • Reconnect after adding a waypoint: long-lived gRPC connections keep the path they were opened on, so a waypoint sees no traffic until callers reconnect (for example by restarting them).
  • Timeouts and delays: a route timeout does not cut off a fault delay injected by the mesh; it only cuts off real upstream slowness.

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text: TinyOlly runs on kind (Kubernetes) inside a Colima VM. First time? Follow the Quick Start.

docs.title: Start
docs.text:
./scripts/colima-up.sh && ./scripts/kind-up.sh
./k8s/02-deploy-tinyolly.sh

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
./scripts/status.sh
kubectl get pods

docs.title: Rebuild from your checkout
docs.text:
./build/local/build-core-kind.sh                                     # core images
kubectl rollout restart deploy/tinyolly-ui deploy/tinyolly-otlp-receiver
./k8s/05-rebuild+deploy-mcp.sh                                       # MCP server (also after editing docs/)
./k8s/06-rebuild+deploy-sre.sh                                       # AI SRE Agent

docs.title: Remove
docs.text:
./k8s-otel-demo/02-cleanup-otel-demo-helm.sh   # the demo only
./k8s/03-cleanup.sh                            # TinyOlly
kind delete cluster --name tinyolly            # the cluster
colima stop -p tinyolly                        # the VM

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: What Address UI (tour) http://localhost:5005 OTLP from your Mac localhost:4317 (gRPC), localhost:4318 (HTTP) OTLP from inside the cluster otel-collector:4317, otel-collector:4318 MCP server (connect) http://localhost:8765/mcp Demo shop and flag panel kubectl port-forward svc/frontend-proxy 8080:8080 AI SRE console kubectl port-forward deploy/tinyolly-sre 7173:8080

docs.title: Size profiles
docs.text:
The scripts pick one from your Mac's RAM. To override, put PROFILE=lean or PROFILE=full before each script.

lean (under 48 GB) full (48 GB and up) Colima VM 8 CPU, 12 GB host cores minus 2, 40 GB Demo load 15 users 40 users and browser traffic Demo components no Kafka, AI components, telemetry-docs or demo OpAMP server all

To resize an existing VM: colima stop -p tinyolly, then ./scripts/colima-up.sh. COLIMA_CPU, COLIMA_MEMORY and COLIMA_DISK override the numbers.

full can drop telemetry

Under full load some batches are lost (database is locked or timeouts in the tinyolly-otlp-receiver log). full is not yet verified on a 64 GB Mac.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Nothing in the UI: wait a minute or two, then check the pods and logs:

kubectl get pods
kubectl logs deploy/otel-collector --tail 20
kubectl logs deploy/load-generator --tail 20

Port already in use: the cluster needs 4317, 4318, 5001, 5005, 8765 and 19291 on your Mac.

VM creation hangs: the VM disk is in ${COLIMA_HOME:-~/.colima}; keep it on an APFS disk.

docs.title: Manifests
docs.text:
The manifests are in k8s/ and pull images from Docker Hub. 02-deploy-tinyolly.sh is the normal way to apply them; by hand:

kubectl apply -R -f k8s/otelcol-configs/
kubectl apply -f k8s/tinyolly-sqlite-pvc.yaml -f k8s/tinyolly-otlp-receiver.yaml -f k8s/tinyolly-opamp-server.yaml \
  -f k8s/otel-collector.yaml -f k8s/tinyolly-ui.yaml -f k8s/tinyolly-mcp.yaml

Do not use kubectl apply -f k8s/: it skips the collector ConfigMaps and also deploys the AI SRE Agent. To publish images, see Development and testing.

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text: The read-only TinyOlly MCP server lets an AI assistant (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Zed, any MCP client) query traces, logs, metrics and the service map, draw charts and follow investigation playbooks. It ships with every TinyOlly deployment: start TinyOlly and point your client at it. What it can do: MCP tools and playbooks.

docs.title: Where it runs
docs.text:
Deployment How it runs URL Kubernetes (kind) A tinyolly-mcp Deployment and NodePort Service (k8s/tinyolly-mcp.yaml, misc/k8s-core-only/tinyolly-mcp.yaml); the kind config maps host port 8765 to it. http://localhost:8765/mcp Standalone You run server.py, or the client starts it over stdio (see below). your choice

All clients share one server over streamable HTTP. It reads TinyOlly through the REST API (TINYOLLY_URL, http://tinyolly-ui:5002 inside the stack), bundles the docs and playbooks, and is reachable only from your Mac.

docs.title: Check that it is up
docs.text:
An initialize call returns JSON listing tools and instructions:

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-03-26","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"check","version":"1"}}}'

Docker: docker ps --filter name=tinyolly-mcp. Kubernetes: kubectl get deploy tinyolly-mcp.

docs.title: Connect a client
docs.text:
Claude Code:

claude mcp add --transport http tinyolly http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp

Claude Desktop cannot reach a local URL (its URL connectors run in Anthropic's cloud), so bridge it with mcp-remote under "mcpServers" in ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json. Use the absolute path to npx (nvm: ~/.nvm/versions/node/<version>/bin/npx) and set PATH, because the app does not load your shell profile. Then quit (Cmd+Q) and reopen it:

"tinyolly": {
  "command": "/absolute/path/to/npx",
  "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp"],
  "env": { "PATH": "/directory/containing/node:/usr/bin:/bin" }
}

Zed: add the URL as a context server, or use the stdio command (Standalone below). Then ask: "pretty print the service catalog".

docs.title: Rebuild after changes
docs.text:
The server is deployed by k8s/02-deploy-tinyolly.sh. After changing docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp or docs/, rebuild it and restart your client:

k8s/05-rebuild+deploy-mcp.sh

A kind cluster created before the 8765 mapping in scripts/kind-config.yaml cannot gain a host port; bridge it instead (Colima docker context):

docker run -d --restart=always --network kind -p 8765:8765 alpine/socat tcp-listen:8765,fork,reuseaddr tcp:tinyolly-control-plane:30876

Run Docker or Kubernetes, not both. When moving from Kubernetes to Docker, remove that bridge, and restart your clients after any switch:

docker rm -f tinyolly-mcp-bridge

docs.title: Standalone
docs.text:
Without containers, the client starts the server over stdio. The installer creates a venv and prints the lines for each client (details):

docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/install.sh

Or run the HTTP server yourself (TINYOLLY_URL points it at TinyOlly, default http://localhost:5005):

python server.py --http --port 8765

Prefer the container: stdio keeps a stale server running until the client restarts.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Old or missing tools: restart the client after a rebuild, and check the container runs the new image.
  • Connection refused on 8765: the stack is down, or the kind cluster predates the port mapping (use the bridge above).
  • Port 8765 in use: the other stack or a leftover tinyolly-mcp-bridge is running.
  • Mesh tools or charts missing: the image is stale; rebuild python-base first, then the MCP image.

docs.title: MCP server (AI agents)
docs.text: docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp is a read-only MCP server. Claude Code, Zed or any MCP client can query your running TinyOlly (traces, spans, logs, metrics, service catalog and map) and read these docs. It has no collector config or admin operations.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Start TinyOlly (UI on http://localhost:5005).

  2. Run the installer. It creates a venv and prints the lines to copy for your client, with your paths filled in:

    docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/install.sh

  3. Connect your client:

Client What to do Claude Code Paste the claude mcp add tinyolly -- ... line the installer printed. Claude Desktop Paste the "tinyolly": {...} entry under "mcpServers" in ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (Settings, Developer, Edit Config), then quit (Cmd+Q) and reopen Claude. Zed Paste the context_servers entry into ~/.config/zed/settings.json.

The client starts the server itself. Check it with "pretty print the service catalog".

Why not just a URL?

Claude Desktop's URL connectors are called from Anthropic's cloud, which cannot reach localhost, so the client starts a local server instead.

docs.title: Always-on server (Docker or Kubernetes)
docs.text: TinyOlly's Docker and Kubernetes deployments also run the server as a container on http://localhost:8765/mcp, shared by every client. See the MCP Server deployment page.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool What it does list_services Service catalog: rate, error rate, p50/p95/p99, worst errors first (format="table" for a table) get_service_map Caller → callee edges with calls, errors, p95. With Istio: node role, edge mtls, source_kind, denied_count; merge=False for the layered view. Filters: service, only (denied, plaintext, errors), limit get_mesh_posture Istio posture: mTLS coverage %, plaintext edges, denied calls find_denied, find_plaintext Only the denied or non-mTLS edges get_edge One edge in detail: RED numbers of both services and the Envoy/ztunnel response flags (UC, UT, DI, DENY...) with their meaning and a next step get_trace_mesh Mesh view of a trace: proxy time per hop, retries, decoded response flags get_version_split Canary view: traffic share, error rate and avg_ms per version, with findings when one version is slower or fails more what_changed Change markers (deploys, policies, scenarios; POST /api/events) and how failures, response flags and traffic changed around each suggest_authz Draft least-privilege ALLOW AuthorizationPolicy from the callers seen (SPIFFE identities), listing plaintext callers it would block. Review before applying chart_map_diff The map coloured by what changed around the latest change marker (red: more failures, teal: fewer, blue: new or busier, grey: quieter) chart_trace_path One trace over the map: numbered hops with time in each, and mesh-proxy time versus app time compare_windows Last N minutes vs the N before: new, gone, more errors, slower search_traces Recent traces by service (any span from it), errors, min duration, root name (format="table") get_trace Bounded summary of a trace: duration, counts, per-service breakdown, error and slowest spans. format="waterfall" draws a text waterfall get_trace_spans Page through a trace's spans (offset/limit, service/error/duration filters) get_span One span in full (attributes, events, links, resource) search_spans Recent spans by service, errors, duration, name (format="table") query_logs Logs by trace, service, severity, substring (format="table") list_metrics Metric names, with a search filter query_metric Time series for the last N minutes, downsampled (min/max/avg/last). labels filters on attributes; group_by sums per attribute value chart_metric Image: line chart of a metric (histograms: mean solid, p95 dashed) chart_service_map Image: the whole map, or with service one service's callers (left) and callees (right), coloured by health, edges labelled with p95 and rate (depth=2 for two hops) list_skills, get_skill Investigation playbooks, and the full steps of one list_docs, search_docs, read_doc These docs: list pages, search sections, read a page or one section

The docs are also MCP resources: tinyolly-docs://<name> (for example tinyolly-docs://quickstart).

docs.title: Pretty output and charts
docs.text:
JSON output is compact for agents. To show a person, pass format="table" (catalog, traces, spans, logs) or format="waterfall" on get_trace (span tree with timing bars; big traces keep every error span and the slowest, up to max_rows). chart_metric and chart_service_map return PNG images (drawn with matplotlib, installed by install.sh), so the client must display images; Claude Desktop and Claude Code do. Desktop shows a small preview: click to enlarge, or ask for a file with save_to ("save the service map to ~/Desktop/map.png").

chart_service_map draws each service as a card with a role icon, err · p95, and a health stripe (blue healthy, amber above 1% errors, red above 5%, grey no connections). With mesh data, edge colour shows security: green mTLS, amber dashed plaintext, red denied or errors, grey unknown. Only the six busiest edges carry latency labels on the whole map.

During a fault the failing services turn red, and chart_trace_path draws one request's journey hop by hop. chart_map_diff needs a mesh: it reads Istio request metrics.

Try: "show me the service map", "draw the service map around cart", "show the slowest checkout trace as a waterfall", "chart http.server.duration for tinyolly-ui".

docs.title: Investigation skills
docs.text:
Seven short playbooks live inside the server (docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/skills/); nothing is installed into the client.

Skill Use it for tinyolly-triage "What is wrong right now?": rank services, find a failing trace, report where/what/evidence/next tinyolly-trace-investigation One trace: summary, waterfall, paging huge traces, self-time vs first error tinyolly-service-deep-dive One service: vitals, dependencies, errors, slow traces, logs, metrics tinyolly-metrics-explorer Finding, charting and reading metrics (counters, gauges, histograms, cardinality) tinyolly-troubleshoot-stack TinyOlly empty or unreachable (Colima contexts, ports, retention), setup questions tinyolly-mesh-investigation Istio mesh: mTLS posture, denied and plaintext edges, mesh time and retries, version split, what changed tinyolly-demo-failure-injection Break the OTel demo with a feature flag and watch TinyOlly catch it

They are offered as tools (list_skills, get_skill(name); the server tells agents to call list_skills first), as prompts with an optional focus argument (for example tinyolly-triage with focus "checkout is slow"), and as resources (tinyolly-skills://<name>). Tests check that every tool and parameter a skill names exists. To add one, create skills/<name>.md with name (the file name) and a description starting with "Use when".

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
The server reads docs/*.md (TINYOLLY_DOCS_DIR overrides it), strips screenshots and HTML, flattens admonitions and tabs, and splits pages by heading so read_doc(name, section) returns only what is needed. list_docs shows each page's title and description front matter, so new pages need it.

Try: "how do I run the OpenTelemetry demo?", "which collector presets exist?", "what ports does TinyOlly use?".

docs.title: Large traces
docs.text:
Nothing returns an unbounded payload. Drill down: search_traces → get_trace (a few KB even for 6,000 spans) → get_trace_spans (pages of up to 200 rows) → get_span. Values and log bodies are truncated, series downsampled, and every response is capped at TINYOLLY_MCP_MAX_CHARS (default 20,000) with a truncated flag that tells the agent to narrow the query.

Try: "which services have the highest error rate?", "find the slowest checkout trace and tell me where the time went", "show error logs for the cart service".

docs.title: Metrics & Cardinality explorer
docs.text: TinyOlly provides a powerful interface for analyzing OpenTelemetry metrics, with specific tools designed to help you understand the shape and cardinality of your telemetry data.

docs.title: Metrics Table
docs.text:
The metrics table offers a dense, high-information view of all ingested metrics.

Click the Chart button to visualize metric data over time:

docs.title: Key Columns
docs.text:
• Name: The full OTel metric name (e.g., http.server.response.size).
  • Unit: The unit of measurement (e.g., By, ms).
  • Type: The metric type (Histogram, Sum, Gauge, etc.).
  • Resources: Click to view the unique resource combinations associated with this metric.
  • Cardinality: Shows the number of label dimensions vs the total number of unique time series (e.g., 8 labels / 185 series).

docs.title: Cardinality Explorer
docs.text: Clicking on the blue Cardinality link for any metric opens the Cardinality Explorer. This tool is essential for understanding "high cardinality" issues and exploring your data's dimensions.

docs.title: 1. Header Stats
docs.text:
• Total Series (Historic): The total number of unique time series seen for this metric since startup (persisted in SQLite).
  • Active Series (1h): The count of series seen in the last hour.
  • Label Dimensions: The number of unique label keys (e.g., http.method, http.status_code).

docs.title: 2. Label Analysis Table
docs.text:
This table helps you identify which labels are contributing most to your cardinality.

  • Label Name: The key of the label.
  • Cardinality: The number of unique values for this label.
  • Values (Top 5): A preview of the most common values.
    • If there are more than 5 values, a clickable ... link expands the list to show all values inline.

docs.title: 3. Raw Active Series
docs.text:
A scrollable view of all active series in a PromQL-like syntax:

{container.id="...", http.method="GET", http.route="/api/traces", http.status_code="200", service.name="tinyolly-ui"}
{container.id="...", http.method="GET", http.route="/health", http.status_code="200", service.name="tinyolly-ui"}

docs.title: Export Actions
docs.text:
Use the buttons in the "Raw Active Series" section to export data for offline analysis:

  • Copy PromQL: Copies the visible series list to your clipboard.
  • Download JSON: Downloads the full series object as a JSON file.

docs.title: Cardinality Protection
docs.text:
TinyOlly includes built-in protection against cardinality explosions to prevent memory exhaustion during local development.

  • Hard Limit: 1000 unique metric names (MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY).
  • Visual Warning: the Metrics tab shows count/1000, which turns red with a ⚠️ at 80% of the limit (the display assumes the default 1000).
  • Behavior: Metrics exceeding the limit are dropped, and a system alert is triggered.

See Cardinality Protection for more details.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Collector
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry Collector configuration management via OpAMP

TinyOlly uses the OpenTelemetry Collector as the telemetry ingestion and shipping layer. The collector receives telemetry from your applications and forwards it to TinyOlly's OTLP receiver.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config Page
docs.text:
TinyOlly includes a web interface for managing OpenTelemetry Collector configurations via the OpAMP (Open Agent Management Protocol). Access this page through the "OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config" tab in the TinyOlly UI.

Features: - View current configuration from connected collectors - Apply configuration changes with real-time validation - Browse configuration templates for common use cases - Monitor OpAMP server status and connected agents - Preview configuration diffs before applying

Requirements: - Your collector must be configured with the OpAMP extension (see OpAMP Configuration below) - Collector must be connected to the OpAMP server

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
TinyOlly includes a sample collector configuration that you can customize for your needs. The configuration files are located at:

  • Source of truth: docker/otelcol-configs/config.yaml
  • k8s/otelcol-configs/config.yaml is a ConfigMap generated from it by scripts/sync-k8s-configs.sh

docs.title: Default Configuration
docs.text:
The default configuration includes:

  • OTLP Receivers: Accepts telemetry on ports 4317 (gRPC) and 4318 (HTTP)
  • OpAMP Extension: Enables remote configuration management via TinyOlly UI
  • Span Metrics Connector: Automatically generates RED metrics from traces
  • OTLP Exporter: Forwards all telemetry to TinyOlly's OTLP receiver, batching it in the exporter's own sending_queue (the batch processor is deprecated; see the OpenTelemetry migration guide)

docs.title: Customization Examples
docs.text:
You can extend the collector configuration to add additional capabilities. The collector uses the otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib image which includes:

  • Receivers: OTLP, Prometheus, Jaeger, Zipkin, and many more
  • Processors: Batch, Memory Limiter, Resource Detection, Tail Sampling, Filtering
  • Connectors: Span Metrics, Service Graph
  • Exporters: OTLP, Prometheus, Logging, and many more

For a complete list of available components, see the OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib documentation.

docs.title: Applying Changes
docs.text:
Either apply a config from the UI tab above (over OpAMP), or edit docker/otelcol-configs/config.yaml, regenerate the ConfigMaps and restart the collector:

./scripts/sync-k8s-configs.sh
kubectl apply -f k8s/otelcol-configs/
kubectl rollout restart deployment/otel-collector

docs.title: Using Your Own Collector
docs.text:
You can use your own OpenTelemetry Collector instance instead of the one bundled with TinyOlly. This is useful if you have an existing collector setup or want to test specific collector configurations.

Deploy the core-only version of TinyOlly (no bundled collector, with the OpAMP server for remote config):

cd misc/k8s-core-only
./01-deploy.sh        # ./02-cleanup.sh removes it

Then, configure your collector's OTLP exporter to send data to the TinyOlly Receiver:

  • Endpoint: tinyolly-otlp-receiver:4343 inside the cluster
  • Protocol: gRPC
  • TLS: Insecure (or configured as needed)

Example Exporter Configuration: 

exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: "tinyolly-otlp-receiver:4343"
    tls:
      insecure: true

docs.title: OpAMP Configuration (Optional)
docs.text:
The OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config page in the TinyOlly UI allows you to view and manage collector configurations remotely. To enable this feature, add the OpAMP extension to your collector config:

extensions:
  opamp:
    server:
      ws:
        endpoint: ws://tinyolly-opamp-server:4320/v1/opamp

service:
  extensions: [opamp]

The default configuration template (located at docker/otelcol-configs/config.yaml) shows a complete example with OTLP receivers, OpAMP extension, exporter-side batching, and spanmetrics connector. Your collector will connect to the OpAMP server and receive configuration updates through the TinyOlly UI.

docs.title: Ask an AI about the OpenTelemetry Demo
docs.text:
Try TinyOlly's MCP server on the OpenTelemetry Demo: real services, traces and logs, and failures you switch on with a flag. Ask an assistant (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Zed) in plain English; it answers from TinyOlly's data.

Before you start: TinyOlly and the demo are running (add the demo), and the assistant is connected to http://localhost:8765/mcp (set up and connect it). "List the TinyOlly playbooks you have" should show tinyolly-demo-failure-injection.

docs.title: Prompts to try
docs.text:
Explore

Prompt Tool "What services are running, and how healthy are they?" list_services "Show me the service map." chart_service_map "Draw the neighbourhood of checkout, two hops out." chart_service_map "How does an order flow through the shop?" search_traces, get_trace

Investigate a failure

Prompt Tool "Something is wrong with checkout. What is failing and why?" get_service_map (errors only), search_traces, get_trace "Show me a failing order as a waterfall." search_traces (errors only), get_trace (waterfall) "Draw the journey of that failing request over the map." chart_trace_path "Explain the edge from checkout to payment: errors, latency." get_edge "Break payments for me, then show how TinyOlly catches it." get_skill → tinyolly-demo-failure-injection

Dig deeper

Prompt Tool "Find the slowest checkout traces and tell me where the time goes." search_traces, get_trace_spans "Show the attributes of the payment span in that trace." get_span "Group traces.span.metrics.calls by service and status." query_metric "Are any card numbers or emails visible in span attributes?" (with the emitRawPii flag on) search_spans, get_span "Which metrics exist for the cart service?" list_metrics

Learn the tool

Prompt Tool "How do I apply the PII redaction preset?" search_docs, read_doc "Which feature flags can I use to break the demo?" read_doc

docs.title: Worked example: payments start failing
docs.text: A real run on kind with paymentFailure at 50%.

docs.title: 1. Break it
docs.text: With the shop port-forward running (kubectl port-forward svc/frontend-proxy 8080:8080), open http://localhost:8080/feature and set paymentFailure to 50%. Errors show within a minute or two.

docs.title: 2. Ask what is wrong
docs.text:
Something is wrong with checkout. What is failing and why?

The catalog shows the two services whose error rate jumped, and get_service_map with only="errors" returns just the failing path (trimmed):

{"nodes": [{"id": "frontend"}, {"id": "checkout"}, {"id": "payment"}],
 "edges": [{"source": "frontend", "target": "checkout", "error_count": 4, "p95": 59.03},
           {"source": "checkout", "target": "payment",  "error_count": 4, "p95": 8.6}]}

docs.title: 3. Look at a failing order
docs.text:
Show me a failing order as a waterfall.

search_traces (errors only, service payment) finds the traces and get_trace draws one (error spans ✗ shown; the tool also lists the slowest spans and how many it hid):

Trace f8ff6711ece8e830e65a3142885cd309: 47.8ms, 100 spans, 7 errors, 9 services
  └ frontend-proxy: router frontend egress   │                   ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│  21.9ms ✗
        └ frontend: executing api route (pa… │                   ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│  21.2ms ✗
          └ frontend: grpc.oteldemo.Checkou… │                   ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ │  20.8ms ✗
            └ checkout: oteldemo.CheckoutSe… │                    ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓ │  19.3ms ✗
              └ checkout: oteldemo.PaymentS… │                               ▓▓▓▓ │  5.09ms ✗
                └ payment: grpc.oteldemo.Pa… │                                 ▓▓ │  1.86ms ✗
                  └ payment: charge          │                                 ▓▓ │   902µs ✗

The failure starts in payment: charge and bubbles up to the proxy.

docs.title: 4. See the journey
docs.text:
Draw the journey of that failing request over the map.

chart_trace_path numbers each hop with its time, failing services in red:

docs.title: 5. Confirm with the edge
docs.text:
Explain the edge from checkout to payment.

get_edge reports 18.18% errors on both ends and a p95 of about 7.5 ms at payment: the failures are fast, so payment rejects charges rather than timing out.

docs.title: 6. Turn it off and check
docs.text:
Set paymentFailure back to off at http://localhost:8080/feature.

A minute or two later new orders stop failing, and the catalog's error rate decays as the window moves on.

docs.title: What the tools do not cover for this demo
docs.text: what_changed lists change markers (such as the flag flips the AI SRE Agent's demo shift records), but its before/after comparison and chart_map_diff read Istio request metrics, so they show no differences for this demo, which has no mesh. The trace-based tools above work.

docs.text:
• Add the Demo and Create Scenarios: setup and failure flags
  • MCP tools and playbooks: every tool and playbook
  • Istio ambient demo: the same ideas for a service mesh

docs.title: 2. Add the Demo
docs.text:
This page adds the OpenTelemetry Demo (Astronomy Shop). It is a web shop of many services with a load generator, sending to TinyOlly.

./k8s-otel-demo/01-deploy-otel-demo-helm.sh
kubectl get pods
kubectl port-forward svc/frontend-proxy 8080:8080

The first run pulls images for a few minutes. Keep the port-forward running. The shop is at http://localhost:8080.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
Within a couple of minutes, services, traces and the service map fill in at http://localhost:5005.

A few errors in the first minutes are normal while pods start.

docs.title: 1. Quick Start
docs.text:
This page gets TinyOlly running on a Mac. It uses Kubernetes (kind) inside a Colima VM. You need an Apple Silicon Mac with 24 GB or more.

brew install colima docker kubectl kind helm
git clone https://github.com/tinyolly/tinyolly && cd tinyolly
./scripts/colima-up.sh
./scripts/kind-up.sh
./k8s/02-deploy-tinyolly.sh
kubectl get pods

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
All pods are Running. The UI is at http://localhost:5005. It is empty until something sends telemetry, apart from TinyOlly itself.

For sizes, ports, cleanup and troubleshooting, see Kubernetes.

Next: Add the Demo

docs.title: 4. Create Scenarios
docs.text:
You break the demo shop. The AI SRE agent from step 3 finds the problem.

You need the shop port-forward from step 2:

kubectl port-forward svc/frontend-proxy 8080:8080

You also need the agent console at http://localhost:7173.

docs.title: Do this
docs.text:
1. Open http://localhost:8080/feature
  2. Set paymentFailure to 50% in its dropdown. It applies at once; there is no save button.

The agent is not told what you changed.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
• Within a few minutes, checkout and payment turn red at http://localhost:5005.
  • The agent adds an investigation to the console list with a name and status.
  • Click it for the cause (payment) and proposed fixes. Fixes are never applied.

Then set the flag back to off. A few minutes later the agent marks the investigation resolved.

docs.title: Flags worth trying
docs.text: flag value what breaks paymentFailure 50% payment errors seen as checkout failures paymentUnreachable on payment is unavailable cartFailure 75% cart errors adFailure on ad service errors imageSlowLoad 10sec slow images intlShippingSlowdown 10sec slow shipping on one path

docs.title: Hands-off
docs.text:
One optional command flips flags on a timer and scores the agent:

./k8s/06-rebuild+deploy-sre.sh --demo

Details in AI SRE Details.

Next: Send Your Own Telemetry

docs.title: Send Your Own Telemetry
docs.text: Point your own app's OpenTelemetry exporter at TinyOlly. This requires step 1, Quickstart.

docs.title: Do this
docs.text:
From your Mac:

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318   # HTTP
# or
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317   # gRPC

From inside the cluster:

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318   # HTTP
# or
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317   # gRPC

From another namespace use otel-collector.default instead of otel-collector.

Also export a service name so it is easy to find:

export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=my-app

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:5005, send some requests, and look for my-app in Traces and Service Catalog.

Next: Your Own Collector Config

docs.title: Data and OTLP
docs.text:
• Ingestion: OTLP/gRPC (primary) and OTLP/HTTP. The OpenTelemetry Collector's config is managed over OpAMP.
  • Storage: traces, logs and metrics in full OpenTelemetry format (resources, scopes, attributes) in embedded SQLite, compressed with ZSTD and msgpack, in WAL mode so reads continue during writes.
  • Retention: records expire after 30 minutes (SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS) and the database is capped at 256 MB (MAX_DB_SIZE_MB, oldest evicted first). Data survives restarts until it expires.
  • Correlation: traces, spans, logs and metrics linked by trace and span IDs; cardinality protection stops metric explosions.
  • REST API: OpenTelemetry-formatted JSON (REST API).

docs.title: UI features
docs.text:
• Trace waterfall with noisy ASGI sub-spans (http send/receive) filtered out, and a per-trace service graph above it; inferred external clients come from orphan parent span IDs.
  • Deep links: ?tab=traces&traceId=..., ?tab=spans&spanId=..., ?tab=logs&search=...; "Copy Link" buttons generate them, and IDs copy with one click.
  • Correlated logs inline in a trace; trace and span IDs in logs jump to their trace or span.
  • Service Catalog: RED metrics; a service name opens a menu (map, traces, spans, logs, metrics) filtered to it.
  • Service Map: Cytoscape.js and dagre, left to right, always fitted to the window. Shape is the service type (server, client, external, database, messaging, isolated, and agent, LLM, MCP server), colour the health (blue, amber some errors, red >5%); TinyOlly's own services can be hidden. With Istio, edges also come from mesh metrics (green mTLS, orange dashed plaintext, red denied), with waypoint and gateway shapes (Istio Ambient Mesh). A selected node shows P50/P95/P99 and rate.
  • Auto-refresh every 5 s, paused while a search filter is active; lists scroll with sticky headers.

docs.title: Agents, LLMs and MCP servers
docs.text:
An LLM such as Ollama and most MCP servers emit no spans, so the call into them is a CLIENT span that nothing answers and the hop would vanish from the map. TinyOlly infers the callee, as it does for databases (tinyolly_common/graph_infer.py):

  • LLM (star): an unanswered call marked agentgateway.outbound.subtype=Llm, or carrying gen_ai.request.model on it or its parent. Named after the gateway route's backend (default/ollama → ollama), else gen_ai.provider.name, else the host. The edge carries input and output tokens, models and endpoints; the label shows tokens per minute.
  • MCP server (chevron): subtype=Mcp or mcp.target. The edge counts calls per method and per tool (gen_ai.tool.name); the label shows the busiest tool.
  • Agent (triangle): a service that makes GenAI calls (a CLIENT span with gen_ai.operation.name, or gen_ai.agent.name). Gateways carry gen_ai.* on their SERVER spans, so they stay gateways.
  • Blocked at the gateway (red edge): a refused call (prompt guard, tool authorization) is an errored SERVER span with protocol llm/mcp, a reason such as Guardrail or Authorization, and no outgoing call. It is drawn to the node it was meant for and counted in blocked; the node's colour includes it.
  • Any other uninstrumented upstream: named by peer.service, the gRPC rpc.service, or the host (a Kubernetes Service name for *.svc.* hosts), unless that is a known service. A call made to an IP is named by reverse DNS, which in Kubernetes gives the Service (10.96.135.219 → cartservice; cached 10 minutes, SERVICE_MAP_RESOLVE_IPS=0 turns it off); IPs without a name and telemetry exports are skipped. SERVICE_MAP_INFER_EXTERNAL=0 turns this rule off.

Inferred nodes have a dashed outline in the UI and in the MCP charts.

Trace detail (/api/traces/{id}) marks those spans with inferredPeer, so chart_trace_path shows the hop too. Built and checked on an agentgateway demo (a shopping agent calling Qwen on Ollama and an MCP fetch tool through agentgateway):

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text:
docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp is a read-only MCP server over the REST API: telemetry queries, these docs (list_docs, search_docs, read_doc), tables, waterfalls and PNG charts, Istio mesh tools, and investigation playbooks served as tools, prompts and resources. Responses are size-bounded; large traces are summarized and paged. It runs as a stdio process started by the client or as the tinyolly-mcp container (streamable HTTP on 8765). See the MCP guide.

The opt-in TinyOlly AI SRE Agent uses these tools to investigate incidents on its own.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Everything runs locally (no CI): ./scripts/test-all.sh runs the unit suites (storage library, UI/API, OTLP receiver, MCP server, frontend JS, OpAMP Go server, collector configs, kubectl guard); --stack adds the end-to-end run against the live stack (88 checks including every collector preset) and --kind a kind smoke test. See the development notes.

docs.title: UI Tour
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:5005.

Traces: each trace's span waterfall with its correlated logs; click a span for its full JSON.

Logs: linked to their trace and span, filterable by severity.

Metrics: every metric with charts and cardinality.

Service Catalog: rate, errors and duration per service; click a name to jump to its map node, traces, spans, logs or metrics.

Service Map: dependencies with shape for service type and colour for health (legend above the map); click a node for latency.

OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config: view a connected collector's config, apply changes with validation and a diff preview, or apply a collector preset (sampling, PII redaction, transforms, connectors and more). The collector needs the OpAMP extension (see OpAMP configuration).
